title: Simulation of a scan across input symbols
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers, an oracle, an input word $x$, and a configuration $c$; fix a register $r$, an integer position $p$, a state sequence $\sigma_j$, and natural numbers $q_0,k$. Suppose $q_0+k\le |x|+1$. Suppose that for every $j<k$ and every tuple of scanned register symbols, the ordinary transition from state $\sigma_j$, reading the input symbol at position $q_0+j$, is the action that moves the input head right, leaves every register tape unchanged and stationary, emits no output, and enters state $\sigma_{j+1}$. Suppose also that there is no oracle call at any state $\sigma_j$ for $j<k$. Then for every $j\le k$, after $j$ steps from the configuration with state $\sigma_0$, input-head position $q_0$, and register-$r$ head position $p$, the run has state $\sigma_j$, input-head position $q_0+j$, and register-$r$ head position $p$, with the other configuration data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A register program $P$, oracle, input $x$, and configuration $c$
A register $r$, integer position $p$, state sequence $\sigma$, and natural numbers $q_0,k$
For every $j<k$ and every scanned-register-symbol tuple, the specified transition is the right-moving, register-idle action entering $\sigma_{j+1}$
No call occurs at $\sigma_j$ for every $j<k$
The conclusion holds for each $j\le k$
